u001.text: , or BigFix [T1072] to deploy the encryptor, gaze.exe, on files across the network—with the actors disabling Windows Defender and other antivirus services on specific targets.

u002.text: (Updated Aug. 18, 2026) Medusa actors use a custom PDQ Deploy playbook to:

u003.text: Run a PowerShell base64 encoded command to exclude the entire C: drive from Windows Defender.

u004.text: Use robocopy to copy gaze.exe into C:\Windows\System32\ via the RunFileCopy.cmd script.

u005.text: Verify if gaze.exe exists, then run it via the command.cmd script.

u006.text: Use command.cmd script to return a print statement indicating if gaze.exe was found.

u007.text: (Updated Aug. 18, 2026) The actors do not use PDQ Deploy for Linux environments.

u008.text: Instead, they use Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) to transfer the encryptor, gaze.py, to the targeted machines.

u009.text: They execute the encryptor using the command nohup python gaze.py &.

u010.text: Medusa actors also make use of an ESXi host profile [T1675] to change root passwords on Linux machines.

u011.text: Encrypted files have a .medusa file extension.

u012.text: The process gaze.exe terminates all services [T1489] related to backups, security, databases, communication, file sharing, and websites, and then deletes shadow copies and encrypts files with AES-256 before dropping the ransom note.

u013.text: Next, the actors remotely turn off [T1529] virtual machines, encrypt them, and delete their previously installed tools [T1070].

u015.text: Medusa RaaS uses a double-extortion model, where victims must pay [T1657] to decrypt files and prevent further release of their data.

u016.text: The ransom note demands victims make contact within 48 hours via either a Tor browser-based live chat, or via Tox, an end-to-end encrypted instant-messaging platform.

u017.text: If the victim does not respond to the ransom note, Medusa actors contact victims directly by phone or email.

u018.text: Medusa operates a .onion data leak site divulging victims alongside countdowns to the release of information.

u019.text: (Updated Aug. 18, 2026) Medusa actors post ransom demands on the leak site with direct hyperlinks to Medusa-affiliated cryptocurrency wallets and claimed number of views.

u020.text: Victims that are still actively negotiating sometimes do not appear on the ransom site, and the Medusa actors use the threat of posting victims as negotiation leverage.

u021.text: Medusa actors offer a “lower rate” for quick payments, stating that discounts will expire after an arbitrary amount of time.

u022.text: Additionally, Medusa actors research victim financial details and base their demands on publicly posted revenue.

u023.text: After a victim pays the ransom, Medusa actors claim to remove the victim’s information from the site.

u024.text: Note: There is no way to verify that Medusa actors remove victim data from the site.
